title: Somatic mutations predict an aggressive phenotype in meningioma but do not drive grade progression

publications.title: Somatic mutation landscape in a cohort of meningiomas that have undergone grade progression

institution: University of Melbourne / Royal Melbourne Hospital
platform: Illumina NovaSeq 6000 (TruSight Oncology 500); Agilent SureSelect Clinical Research Exome V2 (subset)
anatomic_location_breakdown: Per the publication abstract, among NF2-mutated tumours 94% were non-skull base (the 94% figure applies specifically to the NF2-mutated subset, not the whole cohort); overall per-sample anatomic location is not broken down in the live EGA dataset metadata
needs_manual_review_reason: NEW RECORD (2026-07-11). Verified live: EGAS00001006585 has a linked pubmed_ids field of null in the EGA record itself; the paper was found independently via web search matching the exact EGA study title and abstract text verbatim (PMID 36882706, 'Somatic mutation landscape in a cohort of meningiomas that have undergone grade progression', BMC Cancer 2023, same 10-patient/50-sample matched pre-/post-progression design, same NF2/STAT6-NAB2/SETD2/TP53/TERT findings described in both the EGA abstract and the paper abstract almost verbatim). Dataset EGAD00001009391 num_samples=63, not 50: per its own live description, '50 meningiomas were sequenced ... using the hybrid capture-based TruSight Oncology 500 (TSO500) ... and 13 of those meningiomas were also sequenced using Agilent SureSelect Clinical Research Exome V2', i.e. 63 total BAM/sequencing-run files represent only 50 unique tissue specimens (13 specimens sequenced twice, once by panel and once by exome). sample_count is set to 50 (unique tissue specimens) rather than the raw num_samples=63 (sequencing runs); confidence marked Medium because of this run-vs-specimen distinction. grade_breakdown (21 grade_1 / 19 grade_2 / 23 grade_3, summing to 63) is taken directly from the live /samples endpoint's phenotype field ('grade1/2/3 meningioma'), which is reported per sequencing run, not per unique specimen, so it does not sum to 50; flagged as an internal inconsistency in the live source itself rather than resolved by guessing. recurrence_annotated / treatment_timepoint_status left false/'Not reported' despite the study concept being explicitly 'matched pre- and post-grade-progression tissue' from the same 10 patients, because the live per-sample metadata only exposes WHO grade (1/2/3), not an explicit primary/recurrent or pre-/post-progression flag per BAM file, so per rule 13 this cannot be confirmed as deposited per-sample outcome/timepoint annotation, only as a cohort-level design described in the abstract text. No controlled vocabulary value cleanly captures 'matched pre-/post-grade-progression' (distinct from simple primary/recurrent); flagged for a maintainer to consider whether treatment_timepoint_status needs an additional value. Only public EGA study/dataset-level metadata was used; the controlled-access sequencing data itself was never accessed, per docs/scope.md. AUDIT 2026-07-12 (external re-verification): (1) anatomic_location_breakdown reworded; the prior '94% non-skull base tumours' presented as a cohort-wide figure, but the paper's abstract (PMID 36882706) actually states 'Mutations in NF2 were identified in 4/10 patients, of these 94% were non-skull base tumours', i.e. the 94% is specific to the NF2-mutated subset, not the whole cohort. (2) sex_distribution added ('4 female, 6 male (10 patients)') from the live /datasets/EGAD00001009391/samples biological_sex field (39 male / 24 female across the 63 sequencing runs, internally consistent per subject_id, resolving to 6 male and 4 female across the 10 unique donors); previously 'Not reported'. grade_breakdown (21/19/23 per sequencing run), sample_count (50 unique specimens vs num_samples=63 runs), patient_count (10) and all other fields re-verified correct against the live EGA API and PubMed this pass.
